expectations.text: Report has all seven sections: Token ledger, Agent timeline, Round-trips, Per-agent friction, User question load, Orchestration self-critique, Recommendations
expectations.evidence: chat_report.md has headings: Token ledger, Agent timeline, Round-trips, Per-agent friction, User question load, Orchestration self-critique, Recommendations (plus a closing Top recommendations section).

'Total subagent tokens: 429,600 across 7 instances and 11 calls.' Matches the sum of the fixture's usage lines. (The report says 11 calls but its own timeline table lists 10; this is a minor inconsistency.)

expectations.text: States plainly that the total session token count is not knowable from inside the session, instead of inventing a number
expectations.evidence: 'The total session token count (the orchestrator's own context and spend) is not readable from inside a skill, so I'm not giving a figure. 429,600 covers subagents only.'

expectations.text: Reports spec-creator was resumed twice and traces the extra rounds to the missing write-back scope question
expectations.evidence: Round-trips: 'spec-creator a1: 2 resumes.' Friction: write-back scope was 'knowable at the start' and not in the initial question set, so it cost an extra SendMessage and user round.

expectations.text: Orchestration self-critique names the duplicate architecture-reviewer spawn (b2) that was stopped via TaskStop
expectations.evidence: Self-critique item 1: 'Duplicate spawn. The orchestrator spawned architecture-reviewer twice (b1, b2)... b2 was then stopped after about 9 s, wasting 4,100 tokens plus the TaskStop call.'

expectations.text: User question load reports 2 AskUserQuestion rounds (3 + 1 questions) and flags the free-text 'Other' answer as a signal options did not fit
expectations.evidence: '2 AskUserQuestion rounds, 4 questions total (3 + 1).' and 'The offered options... did not fit the real decision... the option set was too coarse.'

expectations.text: Flags implementation-planner re-reading INSIGHTS.md / onion skill as duplicated work
expectations.evidence: Friction: 'It re-read server/INSIGHTS.md and the onion-architecture skill from scratch... That is duplicated work.'

expectations.text: Recommendations are split into prompt wording / orchestration process / tooling-automation buckets and name specific files
expectations.evidence: Three buckets: 'Prompt wording', 'Orchestration process', 'Tooling/automation gap'. Files named: .claude/agents/spec-creator.md, implementation-planner.md, implementer.md. The tooling bucket says 'No clear gap', which is acceptable.

expectations.text: Report ends with the top 1-3 recommendations, not a long list
expectations.evidence: Final section 'Top recommendations to act on' has 3 numbered items. Item 3 bundles two ideas, but it is still 3 entries.

expectations.text: Ledger file created at docs/retro/ledger.md with a header and an entry containing Scope, Agents, Tokens, Friction, Recommendations fields
expectations.evidence: outputs/docs/retro/ledger.md has the header '# Workflow retro ledger' and a 2026-10-04 entry with **Scope:**, **Agents:**, **Tokens:**, **Friction:**, **Recommendations:**.

expectations.text: Did not run in --deep mode (no attempt to read subagent output files)
expectations.evidence: Report states 'no --deep; in-context data only. Subagent transcripts were not read.' Nothing in the report suggests subagent output files were read.

claims.claim: About 1,340 s of agent time, about 45% of it the first implementer run
claims.evidence: 96+41+30+140+612+71+9+98+84+55 = 1236 s, not 1340. Implementer first run is 612 s, which is 49.5% of 1236. Both figures are slightly off.
The fixture and the report's own timeline table show 10 calls.

claims.claim: test-writer never ran; unclear whether that was deliberate
claims.evidence: No test-writer call in the fixture. The report hedges appropriately.

suggestions.reason: Passes, but nothing checks the secondary numbers. The report miscounted calls (11 vs 10) and total duration (1,340 s vs 1,236 s). Consider an assertion on call count (10) and total duration.

suggestions.assertion: Report ends with the top 1-3 recommendations, not a long list
suggestions.reason: Item 3 packs two separate recommendations into one entry. Tighten the assertion to 'at most 3 distinct recommendations'.

No assertion covers the missing re-review after the CRITICAL fix, or the test-writer skip. Both are real orchestration gaps the report found. Add an assertion for 'no architecture re-review before plan-verifier'.
The 'did not run --deep' assertion cannot be verified directly without a transcript. It can only be inferred from the report's own statement.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions check presence and the key numbers well. They are weak on derived figures such as duration and call counts, and they don't cover several valuable findings.
